CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing and chest pain with swallowing for several weeks.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports dysphagia for several weeks, particularly with larger pieces of food. Pain occurs with most foods but not every time he eats. Describes substernal chest pain associated with swallowing. Patient attributes recent stress to relocation from west coast to east coast over the last couple of months. Has been consuming larger quantities of pizza and burgers during this stressful period. Denies weight loss; reports weight gain instead. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stools. Endorses occasional epigastric abdominal pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, nausea, or vomiting. Denies diarrhea. Denies blood in stool or dark tarry stools. Endorses occasional epigastric pain. No other symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is relocating from west coast to east coast, which he reports as a source of significant stress. Has been consuming pizza and burgers frequently. Concerned about transporting his dog during the move and planning to drive rather than fly.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 133/70, heart rate normal, afebrile, oxygen saturation 100%, respiratory rate 19. Weight gain of 10 pounds over the last month noted. Mouth exam: no ulcers, no thrush, tonsils midline. Neck: no adenopathy, no thyromegaly. Abdomen: nondistended with active bowel sounds. Pain to palpation of epigastric area. Negative Murphy's sign, no peritoneal signs, no rebound. Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally. Skin: no rash, lesions, or bruising. Eyes: equal and reactive to light.

RESULTS
Barium swallow showed two areas of mild narrowing in the mid and lower portions of the esophagus consistent with esophagitis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Acute esophagitis. Prescribed Protonix 40 mg once daily in the morning. Prescribed Carafate 1 gram four times daily for one month to coat esophageal and gastric lining. Advised dietary modifications: decrease alcohol and caffeine intake, avoid citrus fruits and spicy foods until symptoms improve, eat slowly and chew food thoroughly. Upper endoscopy scheduled for next week. Follow-up visit next week. Patient counseled on importance of healthy eating and lifestyle changes post-relocation.
